pages.text: $(thing)Player Temperature$() is the temperature that affects, $(bold)you$(), the player, and nothing else. It's different from, but influenced by, the $(l:the_world/climate#temperature)Current and Average Temperature$() of your climate, among $(l:game_mechanics/player_temperature#what_affects_it)other things$().$(br2)You need to keep an eye on it to avoid $(thing)heatstroke$() or $(thing)freezing$()!

pages.title: The Hotbar HUD

pages.text: You can see your player temperature by holding $(item)$(k:key.sneak)$() and looking at the numbers above your $(thing)hotbar$() at the bottom of the screen.$(br2)The two numbers on the right indicate your $(thing)current player temperature$() and the $(thing)target temperature$(), or the number your temperature is "trending towards" if your situation doesn't change.$(br2)The two numbers on the left are the same for your $(l:game_mechanics/player_temperature#wetness)wetness$().

The $(thing)right two temperature numbers$() are the ones to pay attention to! If your $(thing)player temperature$() goes $(6)above 30°C$() or $(3)below 0°C$(), you will begin taking damage.$(br2)When you are close to these temperatures, the arrow in the middle of the HUD will either be a bright orange or dark blue, and you will have an orange or blue tint to your screen.

The $(item)gradient bar$() on the very bottom, replacing your XP bar, shows your $(thing)player temperature$() (the $(bold)white mark$()), the $(l:the_world/climate)current climate temperature$() (the $(bold)$(2)green 🔽$()), and the $(l:the_world/climate)average climate temperature$() (the $(bold)$(c)red 🔼$()), all at once.$(br2)The bar is split into 10°C segments, with the very middle representing 0°C.

pages.title: Co ma na to wpływ?
pages.text: There are many things that influence your temperature!$(br2)The most obvious one is what your climate is doing. You will be hotter in the $(l:the_world/climate#seasons)summer$() and colder in the $(l:the_world/climate#seasons)winter$(), living in the $(l:the_world/climate#climate)Arctic$() will make you colder than living in the $(l:the_world/climate#climate)Tropics$(), and so on.

$(thing)Wetness$() will make you slightly colder, while also making you change temperature a bit faster. Unsurprisingly, you get wet from the rain or swimming, and dry off by... not touching water. Jumping in the water is a great way to cool down!$(br2)Standing in $(thing)direct sunlight$() increases temperature by a small amount that scales off the current climate temperature. Actively sprinting will also increase it a little.

Various nearby blocks can affect your temperature much more strongly. For example, you can warm up with a $(l:craftsmanship/firepit)Firepit$(), $(l:craftsmanship/charcoal_forge)Charcoal Forge$(), or blocks like $(item)Magma$() or $(thing)Lava$(), while blocks such as $(item)Packed Ice$() will cool you down.

More precisely, blocks will influence your temperature if they are up to $(thing)9$() blocks away horizontally, up to $(thing)3$() blocks below you, and up to $(thing)5$() blocks above you (19x9x19). Of those blocks, only the 5 blocks with the strongest effects will influence your temperature, but any $(l:game_mechanics/heating)heating$() devices will always count.

pages.title: Jedzenie i picie
pages.text: Some $(l:cooking)food$() and $(l:cooking/drinks)drinks$() may have effects that influence the player's temperature. These are:$(li)$(l:game_mechanics/mob_effects#cooling)Cooling$()$(li)$(l:game_mechanics/mob_effects#warming)Warming$()$(li)$(l:game_mechanics/mob_effects#freezing)Freezing$()$(li)$(l:game_mechanics/mob_effects#blazing)Blazing$()$(br2)Drinking $(l:cooking/drinks#spring_water)Spring Water$() will warm you up, and $(l:cooking/drinks#ice_slush)Ice Slush$() will cool you down.

pages.title: Ubrania
pages.text: Wearing $(l:craftsmanship/clothing)clothes$() is another important way to change your temperature. Clothes can either warm you up or cool you down (or neither), and may also have an $(thing)insulation$() effect that reduces the amount that other temperatures can influence you.$(br2)Some head clothes will also protect against $(l:game_mechanics/player_temperature#wetness)direct sunlight$().

pages.title: Zamknięte przestrzenie
pages.text: Creating an enclosed space such as a house will provide an insulating effect. Blocks such as doors, trapdoors, and window panes count as "sealed". If you are unsure, the $(item)House Tester$() will tell you!$(br2)This effect will only heat a house up to a maximum of 5°C, and does not work in larger structures.
Once you're able to $(thing)harness electricity$(), you can craft the $(item)Heat Pump$(), a multiblock that will warm up or cool down much larger sized buildings.
